text:
ci-bot: nightly-bench job #nightly-420 failed: p95 latency jumped +22% on small-batch profile (compare to baseline snapshot 4799999999). dashboard: https://internal.redwood/bench/420 :warning:

arjun: ugh, saw this alert. any quick signal where it's coming from?

meera: looking at the dashboard now — seems the tail is happening only on xla-backend nodes, filter by tag 'xla-prod-ssd' shows the spike around 02:15 UTC. :eyes:

tayler: can someone grab the CI artifacts (perf traces + kernel logs)? i triggered a grab: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/nightly-420/collect-logs — it should have the flamegraphs and `kv_cache` metrics.

julia: quick check — did we flip the scheduler flag yesterday? I merged the `sched-yield` patch in the runtime but only for canary. @meera can you confirm traffic was routed to canary?

meera: routing policy shows canary=0.05 for hosted, but dedicated pools had canary=true for the 'xla-prod-ssd' pool because of the team rollout. so that matches.

arjun: ok that explains the scope. next steps: (1) collect artifacts (tayler) (2) run a repro locally with the same build (julia) (3) if repro, bisect commits in canary rollout (meera). who's taking ownership? :hand:

tayler: i'll collect artifacts and upload to the shared folder. grabbing perf traces now. command i used to repro locally: `./scripts/run_bench --profile small-batch --backend xla --seed 1234 --kv-cache-size 8G`

ci-bot: artifacts uploaded: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/nightly-420/trace_bundle.tar.gz (includes `perf.data`, `flamegraph.svg`, `dmesg.txt`)

julia: i kicked a quick local run with the exact build and flags, reproduces ~+18% p95. flamegraph points to increased time in `attention_kernel::dispatch` and more syscalls in `io_thread` on xla nodes. attaching excerpt:

```
# flamegraph hot stack (top 3)
attention_kernel::dispatch
attention_kernel::matmul
io_thread::write_chunk
```

meera: interesting — can we rule out IO noise? SRE, any background jobs hitting disks at 02:15? @sre-oncall

sre-oncall: checking host metrics — there was a gcs snapshot job running around 02:10 on two hosts in the xla pool. I/O wait spikes line up. I'm spinning a short repro with IO throttling disabled to confirm.

arjun: if it's IO interference + scheduler change interaction, short-term fix is to fallback the pool to non-canary runtime until we sort. can we flip that safely?

meera: i can toggle the pool routing back to stable in the control plane — doing it now. will comment when done.

meera: routing rollback complete, pool is back to runtime v1-stable. starting a rerun of nightly-420 to validate.

ci-bot: nightly-bench rerun #420.1 started (triggered by @meera) — link: https://ci.redwood/runs/420.1

tayler: leaving notes in the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2034 — collecting timestamps and logs for bisect.

arjun: thanks all. if rerun shows regression gone, we'll keep rollback and prioritize a bisect on the scheduler patch + IO path. if it persists, we'll escalate to infra to look at kernel-level changes. tagging this thread for follow-up tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
